title: Semisimple algebraic groups are perfect
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $H$ be a semisimple affine $F$-group scheme. Then $H^{\mathrm{der}}=H$. Here semisimple means smooth, connected, affine, of finite type, and having no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme; solvable means that successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. The derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]: the semisimple group $H$ is reductive and has a split maximal torus $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup] to the given smooth connected affine finite-type group $H$; its derived subgroup $D=H^{\mathrm{der}}$ exists and is a closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors.

source.place: Corollary 21.50, printed p.440; Proposition 6.18 and Corollary 6.19, printed pp.129--130

proof.text: For this split reductive pair $(H,T)$, [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] supplies the root subgroups $U_\alpha$, their additive parametrizations $u_\alpha$, and coroots $\alpha^\vee$ with $\alpha\circ\alpha^\vee(s)=s^2$. Conjugation by $t\in T(A)$ sends $u_\alpha(a)$ to $u_\alpha(\alpha(t)a)$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$.

Choose $s\in F$ with $s^3-s-1=0$, using algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Then $s(s^2-1)=1$, so $s\ne0$ and $c=s^2-1\ne0$, in every characteristic. Fix a root $\alpha$ and set $t=\alpha^\vee(s)\in T(F)$. The conjugation formula of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] and additivity of $u_\alpha$ give, over every commutative $F$-algebra $A$,
$$[t,u_\alpha(a/c)]=u_\alpha(s^2a/c)u_\alpha(-a/c)=u_\alpha(a).$$
Thus the morphism $u_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\to H$ is the composite of $a\mapsto(t,u_\alpha(a/c))$ with the commutator morphism. The latter factors through $D$ by [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup], so the inclusion $U_\alpha\hookrightarrow H$ factors through $D$. This is a factorization of scheme morphisms, proved over all $A$, and does not rely on equality of rational-point sets.

source.place: Corollary 21.50, printed p.440, with the torus conjugation calculation from 21.19, printed p.431

proof.text: The closed subgroup $D\subseteq H$ contains every $U_\alpha$ by the preceding step. Apply [lem-sfb-semisimple-root-subgroups-generate] with $G=H$, the same $T$ and $K=D$. Its hypotheses hold because $H$ is semisimple and reductive and all these inclusions factor through $D$. It follows that $D=H$, as asserted. If there are no roots the same generation statement applies to the empty family.
